CausalChain: Iron overload in liver -> increased labile iron fuels the Fenton reaction -> excessive ROS production leads to mitochondrial lipid peroxidation -> dysregulation of mitochondrial iron uptake due to suboptimal mitoNEET function -> amplified lipid peroxidation triggers ferroptosis in hepatocytes -> hepatocyte death exacerbates liver injury; therefore, enhancing mitoNEET function can dampen this cascade.
Hypothesis: Enhancing mitoNEET (CISD1) activity in hepatocytes will reduce mitochondrial iron-induced lipid peroxidation and thereby prevent ferroptotic cell death, offering a novel therapeutic strategy for liver injuries associated with iron overload.
Abstract: Iron overload in liver diseases such as ischemia‐reperfusion injury and non‐alcoholic fatty liver disease contributes to hepatocyte death through ferroptosis—a regulated, iron-dependent form of cell death characterized by lipid peroxidation. MitoNEET (CISD1), an outer mitochondrial membrane protein, plays a critical role in managing mitochondrial iron uptake and oxidative metabolism. We propose that enhancing mitoNEET function can stabilize mitochondrial iron homeostasis, thereby reducing the generation of reactive oxygen species via the Fenton reaction and limiting lipid peroxidation. This, in turn, would mitigate the onset of ferroptosis and attenuate liver injury. Our hypothesis lays the groundwork for novel therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating mitochondrial iron dynamics to protect hepatocytes under conditions of pathological iron overload.
